newsitem.title: NIGERIA: Nigerian oil shares higher despite fuel scarcity.
newsitem.headline: Nigerian oil shares higher despite fuel scarcity.

text.p: Shares of oil marketing firms rose in Nigerian stock trade on Wednesday despite a fuel scarcity in the commercial capital.
The stocks rose to new heights, raising the all-share index to 8270.04 from 8210.43 on Tuesday.
Traders said the latest shortage, reportedly resulting from a dispute among tanker drivers, was having no negative impact on shares of marketing companies.
"There is an incredibly elastic demand for oil shares in this market because of the perception that they are the safest bets," said one.
National Oil rose 29 kobo to 60.71 naira, closely followed by African Petroleum with 25 kobo to 58.70 naira.
But food shares witnessed more robust gains on their current impressive showing. Investors thirsty for more Nigerian Bottling Co shares boosted its by 45 kobo to 49.30 naira.
Cadbury rose 35 kobo to 36.55 naira while Nestle ended 30 kobo higher at 65.60 naira.
Conglomerates also resumed their recent bull run. Franco-Nigerian group CFAO garnered more than four percent or 15 kobo to 3.30 naira, confirming buyers were shopping for them again.
The stock fell substantially last year following a rights issue which backfired as it encouraged investors to take their profit.
PZ Industries was also up 15 kobo at 25.40 naira but Lever Brothers shot up 40 kobo to 24.40 naira, the same as at 14.40 naira.
Banks continued to soar on current positive perception. First Bank was 23 kobo dearer at 17.03 naira and UBA gained 30 kobo at 12.70 naira.

Laggards were led by National Salt Company of Nigeria (NASCON), down six kobo to 6.20 naira. Building materials firms Ceramic Manufacturers dropped one kobo to 25 kobo and Benue Cement fell three kobo to 5.57 naira.
West African Portland Cement Company strengthened to 62.50 naira, up 30 kobo due to undiminished demand.
